videos.why: Moved above rank's 7.2: a famous athlete who became a billionaire through what he owns. A secret_of_rich story with sourced Forbes figures ($40M career pay against $1.6B), the kind of topic behind every 1K+ Short and the owner's picks.
strengths: Famous name and a billionaire question in the first frame, answer held back
Clear before/after: $40M of NBA pay, $1.6B from owning
Payoff splits salary vs fortune and asks the viewer a question
risks: Plain-title test: the title doesn't name him
Board style (still being tested); the payoff stamp covers the top of the hoop

videos.why: A strong how-they-make-money reveal with real SEC figures: American Express paid Delta $8.2B, more than Delta's $6.2B pre-tax profit. A notch below the Magic Johnson Short because it rests on a comparison rather than a person's story.
strengths: Famous company, sourced figures from Delta's 8-K
The turn reads on mute ($8.2B FROM AMEX vs $6.2B PRE-TAX PROFIT)
Cover shows the hidden payer and $8.2B
risks: The board cuts the source line short (template fallback)
The miles framing simplifies what the Amex payment covers

videos.why: A relatable bank story with one sourced JPMorgan figure ($95.44B interest gap, $261.5M a day). The hook is more abstract than the other two, and the first half runs on assumed rates.
strengths: Follows one saver's $10,000 to a borrower: the picture follows the words
The per-day figure is a strong turn
risks: Hook 'Your money, held for free?' is weaker than a famous name
The JPMorgan headline card is plainer than the shot beats
Taste: the owner marked a borrowing-versus Short stale
